name: The trodden lanes down the town's block alleys

documented_range.note: Dated to the scene: every lane is worn by the yards standing on it.

existence.note: RECONSTRUCTED (T-2095, docs/LIBERTIES.md). No source says which 1835 blocks were alleyed, where the alley ran or that it was worn: the strip is the plat model's own mid-block alley (thompson_lots.json `module.alley_note`, itself reconstructed), and a lane is drawn down it only where a structure stands on the block to wear it. The owner asked on 2026-10-04 for the alleys to read as used ground and not prairie (T-2087). No fence is claimed.

ground.note: One ring per lane piece: a band 2.4 m wide down the plat strip's own centreline (narrower where the strip is, leaving 0.6 m of turf each side), its edges wandering 0.22 m over 9.0 m, carried at each end across the corridor to the cross street's track when one lies within 16.0 m and 0.4 m onto it, widening 1.2 m each side over the last 4.0 m; 1.5 m past the block edge where the cross street has no track. Cut where a committed footprint grown by 0.5 m stands across it. Reconstructed — bounded by the plat strip and a cart's track.

left_in_turf.why: no structure stands on this block on the scene date, so nothing wears its alley
